tasks.title: Widen PodStatus with 'closed': pin migration 1's status list, add migration 3, and prove an already-migrated database is not rewritten
acceptance: THE UNION IS WIDENED EXACTLY AS SECTION 5 OF THE FROZEN `contracts/pod-lifecycle.ts` SPECIFIES. `src/shared/contracts/events.ts:60` becomes `export type PodStatus = 'closed' | 'idle' | 'running' | 'waiting' | 'beached';` — `'closed'` FIRST, because it is every Pod's initial state and because two implementers must not produce two orderings. Its docblock states the meaning of all five values in the contract's terms, including that `'idle'` is NARROWED to mean open-and-between-turns, that `'closed'` and `'beached'` both mean no-runner, and that `'beached'` is distinguished by carrying a cause. `LaneStatus`, `LaneKind`, `EventType` and `PermissionMode` are unchanged, character for character.

PIN MIGRATION 1'S POD-STATUS LIST — THIS IS THE CRITERION THE WHOLE TASK EXISTS FOR. `src/main/store/schema.ts` gains `const MIGRATION_1_POD_STATUSES = ['idle', 'running', 'waiting', 'beached'] as const;` beside `MIGRATION_1_PERMISSION_MODES` at `:102`, with a docblock in the same terms (NEVER EDIT; a change to the status set is a NEW migration), and line 147 changes from `${sqlIn(POD_STATUSES)}` to `${sqlIn(MIGRATION_1_POD_STATUSES)}`. It carries NO `satisfies readonly PodStatus[]` clause — the whole point is that it must NOT track the union, exactly as `MIGRATION_1_PERMISSION_MODES` does not. `MIGRATION_2` IS NOT EDITED AT ALL: `schema.ts:243` already writes its status CHECK as a literal and a previous session got that right.

MIGRATION 3 EXISTS AND REBUILDS `pods` WITH THE FIVE-VALUE CHECK, per contract section 6.3. It uses the same table-rebuild procedure as migration 2 (create `pods_new`, INSERT ... SELECT, DROP, RENAME) because SQLite cannot ALTER a CHECK constraint. Both of its constraint lists are PINNED constants local to migration 3: `MIGRATION_3_POD_STATUSES = ['closed', 'idle', 'running', 'waiting', 'beached']` with `satisfies readonly PodStatus[]` (it is the schema head and must stay exhaustive), and `MIGRATION_3_PERMISSION_MODES` repeating migration 2's four modes VERBATIM rather than reusing `MIGRATION_2_PERMISSION_MODES`, which is frozen to migration 2. `MIGRATIONS` becomes `[1, 2, 3]`; `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` follows to 3 on its own because it is computed.

MIGRATION 3 BACKFILLS NOTHING. It widens the constraint and changes no row's status. The `'idle'` -> `'closed'` transition is the boot sweep's job (T2), because the sweep also orphans the lanes and writes the durable `system` event, and doing half the state change in silent SQL would produce rows that changed with no transcript record. A test asserts that after `migrate()` on a seeded v2 database, every pod's `status` column is byte-identical to what it was before.

THE FOREIGN-KEY CASCADE TRAP IS PROVEN CLOSED FOR MIGRATION 3, NOT ASSUMED FROM MIGRATION 2. `lanes.pod_id` and `events.pod_id` are `REFERENCES pods(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`, so with FK enforcement on, `DROP TABLE pods` empties the store and the migration reports success. A test migrates a v2 database holding lanes and events, then asserts the lane COUNT and the event COUNT are unchanged and `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` returns empty. A test that only checks the pods table does not satisfy this criterion.

THE SCHEMA-HEAD GUARD IS ADDED. `schema.ts` gains the exact analogue of `_UncoveredAtSchemaHead` (`:120-127`) for pod status against `MIGRATION_3_POD_STATUSES`, so a SIXTH status breaks the build there and demands migration 4 rather than failing as a runtime CHECK violation on a user's machine. The report states explicitly that the pre-existing `_UncoveredPodStatus` guard at `:65-78` is WEAKER THAN IT LOOKS — an empty array literal is assignable to any array type, so it does not fail on a missing member — that it is kept but not relied on, and that the new `Exclude` plus the tests below are the real guard.

`tests/unit/store/migration-2.test.ts` IS THE TRIPWIRE AND IT MUST BE SEEN PASSING WITH THE UNION WIDENED. It renders migration 1 from the shipped git blob `96f6e925f75c9b101903116a0522c98971e0f347` and asserts byte-identity against the current module. With the pinning done it passes; without it, it renders five statuses and fails. THAT FILE IS EDITED ONLY AT ITS SCHEMA-HEAD ASSERTIONS — `:116-117` (`MIGRATIONS.map(m => m.version)` and `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION`), `:288` (`MAX(version)`) and `:413` (`COUNT(*)`) — which become `[1, 2, 3]` and 3. NOTHING ELSE IN IT MAY CHANGE: not the byte-identity assertion, not the three-permission-modes assertion, not `SHIPPED_MIGRATION_1_BLOB`, not `ENUM_NAMES`, not `shippedMigration1()`. The report quotes the diff of that file in full. An edit anywhere else in it means an enum was widened without being pinned, and that is a BLOCKING finding rather than a test to adjust.

AN ALREADY-MIGRATED DATABASE IS PROVEN NOT REWRITTEN, following the fixture pattern at `tests/unit/store/migration-2.test.ts:45-67` and `:152-163`. A database at `schema_version = 2` with real rows in all three tables is migrated, and the test asserts: only version 3 was appended, the `applied_at` values of the version-1 and version-2 rows are UNCHANGED (proving those migrations were not re-run), and every pod, lane and event row survives with byte-identical column values.

THE CHECK ACTUALLY WIDENED, PROVED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. After migration 3, `UPDATE pods SET status = 'closed'` succeeds and `status = 'sunk'` still fails with `CHECK constraint failed`. The negative half is what proves the constraint was rebuilt rather than dropped. `tests/unit/store/schema.test.ts:106,113` — the test NAME and the accepted-value loop — are updated to cover all five statuses, and the rejected literal stays rejected.

FRESH AND UPGRADED DATABASES CONVERGE. A database created from scratch (1 -> 2 -> 3) and one upgraded from v2 produce the same `sqlite_master` text for `pods`. This is the assertion that catches a MIS-pinned migration 1, because a wrong pin makes the two diverge and nothing else in the suite would notice.

A NEW POD IS BORN CLOSED. `sqlite-event-store.ts:171`'s INSERT literal changes from `'idle'` to `'closed'`: a Pod that has never been opened has no process and its tab must offer `Open`. `tests/unit/store/pods.test.ts:20,69-72,112-115` are updated for the new initial value; the invalid-status rejection test is kept and still rejects. No other column default changes and `CreatePodInput` gains no field.

NO NEW STORE METHOD AND NO NEW COLUMN. `EventStore`'s surface is unchanged, so `STORE_METHODS` in `schema.test.ts` is untouched. `POD_PATCH_COLUMNS` (`sqlite-event-store.ts:61`) is unchanged. `rows.ts:86`'s `row.status as PodStatus` cast stays as it is — the report notes that SQLite's CHECK is the ONLY runtime enforcement of the status set anywhere in the product, which is why the migration work above is not optional, and does NOT add a validator, because adding one is a design change this session did not license.

`npm run typecheck:node` is green and every suite under `tests/unit/store/**` is green at this task's commit. `npm run typecheck:web` IS EXPECTED RED and the report says so precisely: the only permitted failures are the exhaustive `Record<PodStatus, string>` at `src/renderer/src/pods/PodTab.tsx:11-16` and the `statusToken(...)` call sites that pass a `PodStatus`, all of which are T5's to close. The report lists the exact error locations, so a later task can prove the set did not grow. Any web typecheck error outside that set is a BLOCKING finding this task must resolve or escalate.

`src/main/pod-manager/**`, `src/main/pod/**`, `src/main/ipc/**`, `src/preload/**` and every renderer file are OUTSIDE this task's ownership and must not appear in its diff. `dependencies` in `package.json` is unchanged.

tasks.title: The IPC surface states that status is authoritative, and a guard test proves no parallel openness field was smuggled back in
acceptance: THE E1 DECISION IS WRITTEN INTO THE CONTRACT AS A PROHIBITION, NOT A HOPE. `src/shared/contracts/ipc.ts`'s `pods` namespace docblock states that `Pod.status` is the SINGLE authoritative field for whether main holds a live runner, that openness is DERIVED from it by `status === 'idle' || 'running' || 'waiting'`, and that no method on this surface may carry a parallel openness field. `PodStatusPush` (`:189-193`) keeps its exact current shape — `podId`, `status`, optional `exitCode`, optional `detail` — and the `/** Present when status === 'beached'. */` comment on `exitCode` stays true and stays put. THIS TASK'S FIRST DRAFT PROPOSED A `PodView` INTERFACE; that shape was NOT approved and must not appear.

THE SIGNATURES DO NOT MOVE. Every method on `OrcastrateApi['pods']` that returns `Pod` today still returns `Pod`: `list`, `create`, `update`, `open`, `reconnect`. `close`, `delete`, `send`, `interrupt` and `setPermissionMode` are unchanged. A type-level test asserts no `pods` method's return type contains a property named `opened`, and a runtime test over the frozen channel constants asserts no reply object carries one. This is the negative guard that keeps the rejected option from returning through a later well-meaning patch.

`INVOKE_CHANNELS` AND `EVENT_CHANNELS` ARE UNCHANGED — still exactly 21 and 6 keys, with the same names and the same values. A test asserts both counts and that every value is unique. This is what keeps the completeness sweeps in `src/renderer/src/__tests__/failure-paths.e2e.test.tsx` and `src/renderer/src/state/store.test.ts` green through this task's commit: this session adds no channel at all.

NO NEW VALIDATOR, AND THE REPORT SAYS WHY. `src/main/ipc/**` gains no status validation: `status` travels OUTWARD only, no inbound payload carries one, and the product's only runtime enforcement of the status set is SQLite's CHECK constraint (T0). Adding a validator here would be a design change this session did not license. A test asserts no `pods` method ACCEPTS a status or an `opened` argument.

THE ARCHITECTURAL FENCE HOLDS. `src/main/ipc/**` still imports neither `electron` nor `node:fs` nor `src/main/beachcomber` nor `src/main/helm`, asserted by the existing source scan. `src/preload/api.ts` still builds every channel from the `INVOKE_CHANNELS`/`EVENT_CHANNELS` constants and never from a string literal.

THE BRIDGE CARRIES THE NEW VALUE VERBATIM. `src/preload/api.test.ts` covers `on.podStatus` delivering `status: 'closed'` across the bridge unchanged, alongside the existing `'idle'` case at `:250-251`. The preload layer is a pass-through and must not learn what any status means.

Every suite in this task's ownership is green — `tests/unit/ipc/` for channels, envelope, permissions and panels — and `npm run typecheck:node` is green. `tests/unit/ipc/pipeline.test.ts` is T2's and must not appear in this diff. `npm run typecheck:web` is expected red with EXACTLY the failure set T0's report enumerated; this task asserts the set did not grow and names T5 as its owner.

`src/main/store/**`, `src/shared/contracts/events.ts`, `src/main/pod-manager/**` and `src/main/pod/**` do not appear in this task's diff. `dependencies` in `package.json` is unchanged (still exactly `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` and `better-sqlite3`).

tasks.title: Startup reconciliation to 'closed', Matriarch revival on open, the manager half of the start-failure reap, and the close-race that Option 3 exposes
acceptance: `PodManager` gains one synchronous public method, `reconcileStartup(): StartupReconciliation`, matching section 2 of the frozen `contracts/pod-lifecycle.ts` exactly in behaviour and in return shape. It is IDEMPOTENT: a second call with no intervening runner writes no row, appends no event, and returns `pods: []`. A test calls it twice and asserts the second call produced zero store writes, using a store spy.

THE SWEEP DOES THE FOUR STEPS IN THE CONTRACT'S ORDER, each with its own test. (a) Every lane with `status: 'running'`, Matriarch and Calf alike, becomes `orphaned` with `ended_at` stamped from the sweep's single `now()`. (b) ONLY when at least one lane changed, ONE `appendMany` per Pod appends a `system` event on the Matriarch lane followed by one `lane_closed` event per orphaned lane, each on its own lane id with `payload.status === 'orphaned'`; a test asserts the resulting `seq` run is contiguous and in that order. (c) EVERY Pod whose status is not `'beached'` becomes `'closed'`. (d) A Pod with no running lane and a `'closed'` or `'beached'` status produces no write and no entry in the result.

STEP (c) IS THE E1 AMENDMENT AND IT IS WIDER THAN THE FIRST DRAFT'S RULE. The first draft rewrote only `'running'` and `'waiting'` to `'idle'` and left `'idle'` alone as already correct. Under Option 3 `'idle'` means OPEN AND BETWEEN TURNS, so at boot — when no runner exists by construction — an `'idle'` row is a lie. A test seeds a Pod at `'idle'` with NO running lane and asserts the sweep rewrites it to `'closed'`, produces NO `system` event for it, and DOES list it in the returned `pods`. A criterion satisfied by leaving `'idle'` Pods alone is not satisfied.

THE `system` EVENT IS NOT EMITTED FOR A PURE STATUS CORRECTION, AND THAT ABSENCE IS TESTED. Because step (c) now touches every non-beached Pod on every boot, emitting a transcript row for each would put a reconciliation notice in every Pod on every relaunch, which trains the user to ignore the one notice that matters. A test seeds two Pods — one with a running lane, one merely `'idle'` — runs one sweep, and asserts exactly one Pod received the event.

`lastActiveAt` SURVIVES THE SWEEP, AND UNDER OPTION 3 THIS IS THE HIGHEST-CONSEQUENCE LINE IN THE TASK. The pod-status write passes `lastActiveAt: pod.lastActiveAt` explicitly, because `EventStore.updatePod` refreshes it to now otherwise (`event-store.ts:128-132`). The sweep now touches EVERY non-beached Pod on EVERY boot, so omitting it would reset every Pod's last-used stamp to boot time on every launch and destroy the field within one session of use. A test seeds a Pod with a `lastActiveAt` days in the past, runs the sweep, and asserts the value is byte-identical afterwards. A test that only checks `status` does not satisfy this criterion.

`beached` IS NOT REWRITTEN TO `'closed'`. A test seeds a Pod at `status: 'beached'` with a running lane and asserts the lane is reconciled while the Pod status and its recorded cause are untouched. Rewriting it would erase why the Pod stopped and would send the user to `Open` instead of `Reconnect` — a data loss, not a fix.

THE DURABLE RECORD. The `system` event carries `subtype: 'startup_reconciliation'` and a `data` object matching `StartupReconciliationData`, whose `reason` is the exact sentence in section 3 of the contract, asserted verbatim by a test. The sentence is NOT reworded — it already names `Open`, which is now also the affordance `status: 'closed'` selects. `EventType` is NOT widened — `subtype` is a free `string` — and both appended events are synthetic, so neither carries `raw`.

RECONCILIATION IS REVERSIBLE, AND THIS IS THE CRITERION THAT MAKES THE SWEEP SAFE. In `#start`, after `#ensureMatriarchLane` and before `router.restore`, a Matriarch lane whose status is not `running` is set back to `running` with NO `endedAt` — clearing `ended_at` and satisfying the `(status = 'running') = (ended_at IS NULL)` CHECK — followed by a `laneChanged` push carrying the refreshed list. Calf lanes are NOT revived. A test runs the sweep, then `openPod`, and asserts the Matriarch lane reads `running` with `endedAt: null` while an orphaned Calf stays orphaned. Without this the sweep is a one-way door and every subsequent Open leaves the rail permanently wrong.

THE STATUS WRITES MOVE TO `'closed'` AT EXACTLY TWO SITES, per the contract's transition table. `closePod` (`pod-manager.ts:287-288`) writes and pushes `'closed'` instead of `'idle'`, and its existing `pod.status !== 'beached'` guard at `:285` is PRESERVED so closing a beached Pod does not erase its cause. `#start`'s success tail (`:348-349`) still writes `'idle'`, whose meaning is now exact. No other status literal in the file changes.

THE CLOSE RACE OPTION 3 EXPOSES IS CLOSED AND TESTED, NOT REASONED ABOUT. `PodRunner.stop()` ends with `#setStatus('idle')` (`pod-runner.ts:392`), which reaches this class's `onStatus` handler (`:657-661`) and writes `'idle'`; `closePod` calls `#dispose` — which calls `stop()` — and only THEN writes `'closed'`. Before this session both writes were `'idle'` and the race had no consequence. REQUIRED: after `closePod` resolves, the persisted status is `'closed'` and no subsequent `podStatus` push for that Pod carries `'idle'`. A test drives a runner whose `stop()` emits `onStatus('idle')` and asserts both. Detaching handlers in `#dispose` is a legitimate fix; relying on the current statement order with no test to notice a reorder is not.

OPENNESS AND THE SESSION REGISTRY NEVER DISAGREE. A test helper asserts that `#sessions.has(podId)` equals `status === 'idle' || 'running' || 'waiting'` after EVERY public method returns — `createPod`, `openPod`, `closePod`, `reconnectPod`, `deletePod`, and a start that failed. This is the single assertion that catches a missed status write anywhere in the class. A beached Pod is never reported open, because `#markBeached`'s callers delete the session first (`:671-674`, `:339-340`).

THE MANAGER HALF OF THE REAP (`pod-manager.ts:336-347`). The `catch` around `session.runner.start(...)` calls `await session.runner.stop()` before `#markBeached`, wrapped so a throwing `stop()` cannot mask the original failure: the error the caller receives is still the start error with its `CWD_MISSING`/`SPAWN_FAILED`/`RESUME_FAILED` classification intact. A test makes `start()` reject and `stop()` also reject, and asserts the caller sees the start error and that `stop()` was called exactly once. A further test asserts the Pod reads `'beached'` after a failed start — never `'idle'` and never `'closed'`, because a failed start is a failure with a cause. This task must NOT assume T3's runner-side half landed; each half stands alone.

THE CALL SITE. `src/main/index.ts` calls `reconcileStartup()` inside `app.whenReady()`, after the `PodManager` is constructed and BEFORE `createMainWindow()`, as one line with no logic — the file's own docblock forbids logic there. A test or source assertion pins the ordering relative to `createMainWindow`, AND pins that it runs after the store has migrated: the sweep writes `'closed'`, which migration 3 must already have admitted, so a sweep before `migrate()` would fail every write. The results must be readable from the store by the renderer's first `pod:list`, and NOTHING may depend on a push arriving, because `sendToRenderers` drops payloads when no window exists.

THE STALE COMMENT IS CORRECTED. `src/main/index.ts:133` currently reads that `status: 'idle'` covers both open-and-quiet and closed — the earliest written evidence of the conflation this session removes. The CODE stays correct (`PodDirectoryProvider` lists every KNOWN Pod regardless of status); the SENTENCE is rewritten to say the distinction now exists and that this provider deliberately ignores it. The Gate 2 decision recorded on `PodDirectoryProvider` is preserved, not reopened.

DESIGN SPEC SECTION 8 GAINS THE MISSING ROW. `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-18-orcastrate-design.md` section 8's failure table gains a row for a lane still open at PROCESS START, resolving to Orphaned, cross-referencing the reconciliation and naming Open as the recovery. The existing turn-boundary row is left intact. Section 4.4's Pod-status enumeration is updated to five values with `'closed'` described as the contract describes it. The edit is confined to those two places and to any sentence they make untrue; it is not a rewrite of the spec.

NO ENUM IS WIDENED HERE AND NO MIGRATION IS ADDED HERE. `src/main/store/**` and `src/shared/contracts/events.ts` do not appear in this task's diff — the widening is T0's, already landed, and this task consumes it. `EventStore` gains no method: the sweep uses `listPods`, `listLanes`, `setLaneStatus`, `updatePod` and `appendMany`, all of which exist. N+1 over Pods is accepted and stated.

`tests/unit/pod-manager/**` is a NEW directory holding this task's sweep tests with its own helpers, so it does not contend with `tests/unit/ipc/helpers.ts`. `tests/unit/ipc/pipeline.test.ts` is updated only where the widened union or this task's changes broke it — including `:349-369`, which filters `PodStatusPush` for `'beached'`. Both suites are green, as is `npm run typecheck:node`. `npm run typecheck:web` is expected red with exactly T0's enumerated failure set; this task asserts the set did not grow and names T5 as its owner.

tasks.title: PodRunner: reap the child a failed start() leaves streaming, and narrow session-id capture to the messages that authoritatively name the session
acceptance: THE LEAK IS FIXED AT THE ONE THROW SITE THAT LEAKS. `pod-runner.ts:190` — the `#ready.promise` rejection — is the only failure path where `#bridge` has already returned and a Claude Code child may be alive; `:162` and `:171` throw before any query exists. After a `start()` that rejects at `:190`: the abort controller HAS been aborted and the input queue HAS been closed. A test asserts both directly through injected doubles, and it must be seen failing against the current code before it is made to pass.

`stop()` STAYS A NO-THROW IDEMPOTENT NO-OP AFTERWARDS. Called after a failed start it resolves, throws nothing, and two successive calls are indistinguishable from one. The current early-return at `pod-runner.ts:379` makes `#abort.abort()` at `:381` unreachable on this path; how that is resolved — a distinct terminal phase, an explicit teardown before the throw, or making `stop()` reachable — is the implementer's choice, provided this criterion and the next two hold.

THE CALLER'S ERROR IS UNCHANGED. The rejection `start()` produces after the fix is identical in type, code and message to the one it produces today, including `CWD_MISSING`, `SPAWN_FAILED` and `RESUME_FAILED` classification and the `resumeRequested` guard in `src/main/pod/errors.ts:55-67`. A test asserts each classification survives. `send`, `interrupt` and `setPermissionMode` after a failed start still throw `NOT_RUNNING` via `#assertRunning`.

THE BUG ARRIVES WITH THE TEST THAT REPRODUCES IT. A test drives a runner whose `#bridge` returns a live stream and whose `initialized()` rejects, and asserts that the stream stops being consumed — i.e. a message pushed after the rejection reaches no handler and appends no event. That is the observable form of 'the child keeps streaming into the store with no owner'.

THIS RUNNER NEVER PRODUCES `'closed'`, AND THAT IS STATED RATHER THAN LEFT TO INFERENCE. `PodStatus` now has five values (T0), but `#status` is the RUNNER's status and a runner exists only while the Pod is open, so `'closed'` is unreachable from inside this class. `pod-runner.ts:392` keeps emitting `'idle'` after `stop()`, `:105`'s initial value stays `'idle'`, `:368`'s `if (this.#status === 'idle') return;` interrupt guard is unchanged, and `tests/unit/pod/lifecycle.test.ts:97,104` keep asserting `'idle'` after `stop()`, untouched. Making the runner emit `'closed'` was considered and rejected at Gate 2: it would race with `PodManager.#dispose`, and closedness is a fact about the manager's session registry, not about a runner that is by then gone. `src/main/pod/**` gains no reference to `'closed'` beyond the docblock that says this.

SESSION-ID CAPTURE — ESCALATION E2 RESOLVED AS OPTION A AT GATE 2, SO SECTION 8 OF THE FROZEN CONTRACT IS BINDING AND UNCONDITIONAL. Capture narrows to `system` messages with `subtype: 'init'` and to `result` messages, with the LATEST such id in a run winning. A `session_id` on any other message type is IGNORED for capture. There is no option B or C to fall back to and nothing here is conditional.

THE TEST THAT MATTERS emits a hook-shaped message carrying a FOREIGN `session_id` BEFORE `system/init`, and asserts the stored id is init's and not the hook's. It fails against today's first-message-wins latch (`pod-runner.ts:107,233-236`), which accepts a `session_id` from any message type because `stream.ts:64-65` applies no filter, and it must be seen red before it is made green. A second test emits two authoritative ids in one run and asserts the LATER one wins.

THE DIAGNOSTIC FIRES. A warn-level log fires whenever a captured id differs from the one already stored, naming both ids and the Pod id. The repo holds NO captured artifact of a run with more than one `session_id` — the three-ids observation from 2026-08-20 exists only as prose in the backlog, and the code is first-wins where the backlog says last-wins — so the next real run must produce the evidence. The log line states what happened and the identifiers needed to find it again, and logs no secret.

THE CONTRACT SAYS WHAT THE CODE DOES. `src/shared/contracts/pod-runner.ts` records the teardown obligation on `start()`'s failure path, the capture rule for `onSessionId`, and the fact that `status` never takes `'closed'`. The existing `resume` correction docblock is left intact. `PodRunnerOptions` and `PodRunnerHandlers` keep their current members; nothing here widens the surface.

`tests/unit/pod/**` and `npm run typecheck:node` are green at this task's commit. `src/main/pod-manager/**` does not appear in the diff — the manager half of the reap is T2's, and this task must not assume it landed. `src/main/store/**` and `src/shared/contracts/events.ts` do not appear either. This task has NO dependency on T0 and may run first; if it lands before T0, `typecheck:web` is green at its commit and the report says so.

NO SLEEPING AND NO WALL CLOCK in the new tests: every wait is on a condition with a timeout, or the operation is made synchronous for the test, per the test discipline. Existing helpers in `tests/unit/pod/helpers.ts` are extended rather than duplicated.

tasks.title: The renderer stops storing openness: delete runtime.opened and derive it from pod.status at one place
acceptance: `PodRuntimeState.opened` IS DELETED, NOT RETYPED. The property is REMOVED from the runtime record at `store.ts:102`. A test asserts the property name does not appear on the runtime shape, so the deletion cannot silently regress into a re-added convenience field. THE FIRST DRAFT'S TRI-STATE `OpenedKnowledge = boolean | null` IS NOT IMPLEMENTED — it was invented to express 'main has not answered yet', a window that Option 3 removes, and a diff introducing it fails this criterion.

ALL SIX ORIGINS DIE AND NONE IS REPLACED BY AN EQUIVALENT WRITE: the initialiser at `store.ts:161`, the three optimistic `opened: true` patches at `:473`, `:533` and `:552`, the `opened: false` after a successful close at `:542`, and the `beached` push's reset at `:357-360`. The `if (push.status === 'beached')` branch in `onPodStatus` is deleted with the field rather than rewritten; the one line that writes `push.status` onto the Pod row stays and is what makes invariant I5 hold.

THE ONE DERIVATION, AT THE ONE PLACE. `derivePodList` (`workspace-provider.tsx:159`) replaces `opened: runtime?.opened ?? false` with `opened: isPodOpen(pod.status)`, where `isPodOpen` is written in the POSITIVE form specified by section 1 of the frozen `contracts/renderer-lifecycle.ts`: `status === 'idle' || status === 'running' || status === 'waiting'`. The comment states why the positive form is required — an unrecognised future status must read as not-open, because offering to type into a Pod that may not be running is the worse error. The old `?? false` also manufactured 'not open' for a merely MISSING runtime record, a different fact wearing the same answer; that failure mode must be gone, not preserved.

THE DELIBERATE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE IS STATED AND TESTED, NOT DISCOVERED. The three deleted optimistic patches made the composer enable INSTANTLY on click, before main answered. Deriving from `status` means it enables when main's reply or push lands. A test asserts the composer does not enable until a reply or push reports an open status, and the report names this as an accepted trade with its reasoning: an enabled composer over a process that failed to start is a worse error than a few tens of milliseconds of a disabled one, and the existing open-in-flight state renders meanwhile.

HYDRATION NEEDS NO SEEDING STEP AND GAINS NONE. `refreshPods` (`store.ts:430-459`) already calls `api.pods.list()` and assigns to `state.pods`; that IS the hydration of openness under Option 3. NO second fetch, NO new state to hold openness, NO follow-up call — a separate openness fetch is a rejected design and its presence fails this criterion. A Pod absent from a later list has its runtime dropped as today; a Pod newly present needs no openness seeding at all.

tasks.title: Present the reconciled state: land the 'closed' label, token and CSS variable, verify the orphaned row freezes, and prove the run control is the named way out
acceptance: THE FIVE-PART WIDENING LANDS IN ONE COMMIT, per section 4 of the frozen `contracts/renderer-lifecycle.ts`, because a partial landing leaves the theme internally inconsistent. (1) `PodTab.tsx:11-16`'s `Readonly<Record<PodStatus, string>> STATUS_LABEL` gains `closed: 'Closed'` — literal per design §2, reading correctly beside the existing `Idle`; the four existing labels including `beached: 'Beached, process stopped'` are unchanged. (2) `renderer-theme.ts`'s `TOKENS` gains `statusClosed: '--oc-status-closed'` beside the six `status*` entries at `:61-70`, AND the frozen `export declare function statusToken(...)` at `:130-134` gains `'closed'` to its hand-written parameter union. (3) `shell/contract-runtime.ts:27-36`'s `AnyStatus` gains `'closed'` and `STATUS_TOKENS` gains `closed: TOKENS.statusClosed`. (4) `styles/tokens.css:42-50` gains `--oc-status-closed`. (5) `pods/PodBar.module.css` gains a `.statusDot[data-status='closed']` rule so a closed Pod's dot does not silently fall through to the base rule.

THE NEW TOKEN IS DISTINCT AND THE SWEEP THAT PROVES IT IS NOT WEAKENED. `WorkspaceLayout.test.tsx:182-186` adds `'closed'` to its status array; its assertion that the token set is DISTINCT (`new Set(tokens).size === statuses.length`) stands unmodified. This is why `--oc-status-closed` cannot simply alias `--oc-status-idle`. The value chosen reads as quiet and inactive and is distinguishable from `--oc-status-idle` without relying on hue alone — the `Closed` label and the `Open` control carry the meaning; the dot only has to not lie.

EXACTLY THREE FILES ACROSS `shell/` AND `styles/` ARE IN SCOPE and the diff is asserted to contain no fourth: `shell/contract-runtime.ts`, `shell/WorkspaceLayout.test.tsx` and `styles/tokens.css`. Everything else under `src/renderer/src/shell/**` and `src/renderer/src/styles/**` stays frozen. `renderer-theme.ts` and `contract-runtime.ts` are a declare/implement pair and must not drift apart.

SYMPTOM 1 IS VERIFIED, NOT REIMPLEMENTED. An orphaned Matriarch lane renders the word `Orphaned` through the existing `LANE_STATUS_LABEL` and `TOKENS.statusOrphaned`, and its `elapsedMs` is FROZEN — a test advances the fake clock and asserts the rendered duration does not change (invariant I6). If this passes with no production change, that is the correct outcome and the report says so: reusing `orphaned` rather than adding a LANE status is precisely what bought it. A diff that adds a new LANE status token, label or branch fails this criterion — the ONE new status token in this session is the POD status `closed`, and nothing else.

SYMPTOM 2 IS VERIFIED WITH THE COPY UNCHANGED. The composer for a Pod main reported `status: 'closed'` is disabled and shows 'This Pod is not running. Open it before sending a message.' verbatim, and `wording.e2e.test.tsx` pins that sentence. THE COPY IS NOT REWRITTEN — it is exactly true of a closed Pod and already names the way out. A Pod main reported `idle`, `running` or `waiting` has an enabled composer, with no `pods.open` invoked.

THE RUN CONTROL IS THE NAMED WAY OUT AND ITS LABELS ARE PINNED. `PodTab`'s `showRunControl = beached || !opened` renders `Reconnect` for a beached Pod and `Open` for a closed one, and both strings plus the accessible name of the control are asserted. `PodsChrome.tsx:55-57` routes `'beached'` to `reconnectPod` and `'closed'` to `openPod`; a test pins that routing so a closed Pod never triggers a resume. The existing focus-restoration effect (`PodTab.tsx:98-111`), which moves focus to the tab when the control unmounts, still passes its test — accessibility floor: focus moves predictably after an action that changes what is on screen.

SYMPTOM 3 IS GUARDED, NOT GUESSED AT. `PodsChrome.tsx:41` calls `actions.closePod`, and no `NOT_RUNNING` throw exists anywhere on that path — `PodManager.closePod` throws only `NOT_FOUND`. A test therefore proves the benign behaviour: closing a Pod with no live runner resolves `{ ok: true }`, leaves the Pod row and its transcript in place, leaves the Pod reading `'closed'` rather than `'idle'`, and surfaces no error text to the user. DO NOT invent a fix for an error you cannot find; if the symptom still reproduces against the built app, report it with the observed text as a finding.

THE RECONCILIATION EVENT RENDERS, AND ITS ABSENCE IS ALSO TESTED. A `system` event with `subtype: 'startup_reconciliation'` renders its `reason` sentence through the EXISTING system-event branch of `TranscriptEventItem.tsx` and does not fall through to an unknown-type branch or an empty row. A second test asserts a Pod that merely went `'idle'` -> `'closed'` at boot gets NO such row — a notice that always fires carries no information, which is why T2 narrowed the emission condition to Pods whose LANES were reconciled.

NO NEW CHROME. No modal, toast, dismissible banner or new panel for reconciliation or for the closed state. The durable transcript row, the already-correct composer sentence, the `Closed` label and the already-present run control are the whole user-facing story. Transcript filtering, a Pod deletion affordance, pinning changes and the pane model are sub-session B and must not appear in this diff.

`hygiene.test.ts` and `wording.e2e.test.tsx` are UPDATED HERE, by the task that changes what they assert, so the repo does not go red between this commit and T6's. No raw length, color or font-weight literal is introduced outside `tokens.css` — every value in TypeScript comes from `TOKENS` — and the existing hygiene rule is not weakened to accommodate the new token.

ACCESSIBILITY FLOOR HOLDS. Every control this task touches is reachable and operable by keyboard alone, color is never the only carrier of Pod or lane status (the `Closed` and `Orphaned` LABELS carry it, which is what makes the new dot color a secondary signal rather than the message), and every disabled control states its reason in text rather than by appearance.

`npm run typecheck:web` IS GREEN AT THIS TASK'S COMMIT, AND CLOSING IT IS THIS TASK'S OBLIGATION. It has been red since T0 widened the union, with a failure set T0 enumerated and T1, T2 and T4 each asserted did not grow. The report states the before and after error counts and confirms the set closed rather than being suppressed — no `@ts-expect-error`, no `as never`, no widening of a type to swallow the error. Every suite in this task's ownership is green, plus `src/renderer/src/state/**`. `src/renderer/src/__tests__/` files other than `wording.e2e.test.tsx` and `hygiene.test.ts` belong to T6; failures there are named in the report with T6 against them.

PRESENTATION COMPONENTS TAKE DATA AND CALLBACKS. Nothing in this task reaches around its props into the store, no component both arranges other components and renders content, and `PodBar` and `PodsChrome` keep their current split. No component re-derives openness from `status` — that derivation happened once, in T4's `derivePodList`, and a second copy here fails this criterion.

tasks.title: The relaunch regression suite, the three-frozen-one-widened enum guard, and the whole-repo green gate
acceptance: THE REPRODUCTION IS THE TEST. A new `relaunch.e2e.test.tsx` drives the exact scenario observed on 2026-08-20: a store seeded with a Pod at `status: 'idle'` whose Matriarch lane is `status: 'running'` with `ended_at: null` and a `started_at` well in the past, a `reconcileStartup()` before the renderer mounts, and a first `pods.list` that the renderer hydrates from. It asserts all three symptoms are gone: the Matriarch row reads `Orphaned` with a frozen duration, the composer is disabled with the pinned sentence and a visible `Open` control, and `pods.close` on that Pod resolves `{ ok: true }` with no error surfaced. It ALSO asserts the Pod now reads `status: 'closed'` — under Option 3 that seeded `'idle'` was itself part of the lie, and a suite that leaves it `'idle'` has not tested the fix that was chosen.

THE OTHER DIRECTION IS COVERED, AND IT IS THE ONE TODAY'S CODE FAILS. The same suite drives a fresh renderer against a Pod main reports as `'idle'` WITH a live session — the HMR and reload case — and asserts the composer is ENABLED, no run control renders, and `pods.open` was never invoked. Both Pods appear in ONE fixture so neither result can come from the renderer guessing a constant.

EVERY TEST HERE WAS SEEN RED FIRST. The report states, per test, what it asserted and against which commit it was observed failing. A test never observed red has not been shown to test anything; a test that would still pass with the reconciliation deleted fails this criterion.

THE ENUM GUARD CHECKS THE RIGHT THING NOW: THREE FROZEN, ONE DELIBERATELY WIDENED. A test asserts that `LANE_STATUSES`, `LANE_KINDS` and `EVENT_TYPES` are byte-identical to the arrays this session started from, and SEPARATELY that `POD_STATUSES` is the five-value array with `'closed'` first, that `MIGRATIONS` is `[1, 2, 3]`, and that `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` is 3. THE OLD FORM OF THIS CRITERION — 'no enum is widened, `MIGRATIONS` is `[1,2]`, version is 2' — IS FALSE AFTER THE E1 AMENDMENT AND MUST NOT BE WRITTEN. The negative guard survives for the three arrays that are still interpolated live into shipped DDL (`schema.ts:155,162,193`); for `POD_STATUSES` the guard moved to T0's proof that migration 1's RENDERED SQL is byte-identical to the shipped blob despite the widening. This test lives in T0's `tests/unit/store/schema.test.ts`, which is NOT in this task's ownership; this task's obligation is to CONFIRM in its report that the guard exists and passes, and to raise a blocking finding if it does not.

WHOLE-REPO GREEN IS THIS TASK'S OBLIGATION AND NOBODY ELSE'S. `npm test` exits 0 and BOTH `npm run typecheck` halves are green at this task's commit. The baseline was 91 test files and 1392 tests on `main`; the report states the new counts and accounts for the delta, including the new `tests/unit/pod-manager/**` and migration-3 suites. Any suite still red is a BLOCKING finding named with the task that owns it, never a suite this task deletes or skips.

`tests/unit/store/errors.test.ts` IS NOT TOUCHED. It is known order-dependent and fails under `--sequence.shuffle`, pre-existing from sub-session 1. It is not this session's to fix and must not be mistaken for a regression this session caused; the report says so explicitly rather than leaving a reader to wonder.

NO EXISTING ASSERTION IS WEAKENED OR DELETED to accommodate this session's changes. `failure-paths.e2e.test.tsx`'s allowlist of invoke channels with no error surface may be updated ONLY where a channel's surface genuinely changed; the set must not silently grow. Its channel-completeness sweep still asserts 21 invoke and 6 push channels, unchanged by this session. `pod-open.e2e.test.tsx:50-53,91,103`'s beached-Pod reconnect path is extended to cover a `'closed'` Pod taking the OPEN path, so the two not-open states are proven distinguishable end to end.

TESTS ARE ISOLATED AND DETERMINISTIC: no shared mutable state, no wall clock, no ambient time zone, no network, no port, no sleeping. Every wait is on a condition with a timeout. Any randomness is seeded and the seed is reported on failure. Each test creates what it needs and leaves nothing behind.
NAMES STATE CONDITION AND OUTCOME and claim no more than the assertions check. A name containing 'works' or 'is correct' fails this criterion.

THE FAILURE PATH IS TESTED, NOT ONLY THE SUCCESS PATH: a reconciliation that finds nothing to do, a Pod that is beached when the sweep runs, a Pod that is already `'closed'` when the sweep runs, and a `pods.list` that fails outright each have a test asserting what the user sees.
